title: Analytical Bounds on Force Window Classification in Nonprogrammable Grip Feedback
content: Non-programmable grip-force biofeedback can reduce dependence on embedded firmware, but component-level simplicity does not ensure valid force classification. This theoretical study develops an analytical framework linking bridge sensitivity, amplifier headroom, comparator hysteresis, filtering, and cue delay. A ratiometric sensing chain is specified using a strain-gauge bridge, distributed gain, buffered low-pass stages, window comparators, hardwired logic, and burst-driven vibration motors. Circuit equations are evaluated deterministically, and filter sensitivity is examined using 50,000 synthetic tolerance samples. An illustrative single-stage configuration exceeds the instrumentation amplifier’s calculated internal gain limit and yields a combined filter cutoff of 5.956 Hz instead of the nominal single-pole value of 15.915 Hz. The revised filter provides a calculated cutoff of 15.783 Hz. A bounded-error analysis gives a sufficient condition for a non-empty force interval that is classified as acceptable independently of comparator history. Extending this result to rate-limited force trajectories incorporates filter memory and an assumed bounded cue delay. These results establish conditional design constraints rather than measured device performance. No hardware, participant, or clinical data are reported. The conclusions concern the stated mathematical model. Device performance, safe operation, and rehabilitation efficacy are outside the demonstrated scope.
